solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Time right to wear this knitted garment

indicators.note: the word this wears, or encloses, the letter for right, like clothing around a body
knitted suggests letters worked together into a new pattern, so the group is rearranged

explanation.surface: A suggestion that now is the moment to put on a hand-knitted top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wear' puts R inside THIS (giving e.g. THRIS), and 'knitted' rearranges those letters to SHIRT, after T. 'knitted' looks like part of the definition but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-shirt is a simple collarless top, a common item of clothing.

clue.text: Demonstrated shiny material

definitions.meaning: protested by occupying a place, the sense of staging a sit-in
a smooth glossy fabric woven from silk or similar fibre

explanation.definitionFit: To sit in is to protest by occupying a place; satin is a glossy woven fabric.

clue.text: Popular lord backing fellow that's easy-going

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: backing means the word for lord is turned to run backwards

parts.note: lud is the courtroom form of lord, as in m'lud
a gent is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A well-liked aristocrat supporting a relaxed chap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns LUD (the courtroom address to a judge) into DUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Indulgent means lenient and permissive, close to relaxed about rules.

clue.text: The Thunderer covering city in brief may be problematic

indicators.note: in a down answer the god's name sits on top of, so covers, the city's letters

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
NY is the short form of New York

explanation.surface: The newspaper nicknamed the Thunderer reporting briefly on a city could cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times newspaper is nicknamed 'The Thunderer', which is the false trail; here it is the god Thor. 'covering' places THOR above NY in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorny describes an issue full of difficulty, like a plant full of prickles.

clue.text: Violent reaction disheartened slanted character

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, the middle letter of the word

parts.note: a backslash is the leaning keyboard symbol

explanation.surface: Someone reacting fiercely after a slanted typed character lost its spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the central S from BACKSLASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlash is a strong adverse public response to some event or change.

clue.text: A morning call bod made in recreational activity

indicators.note: made here means fashioned or constructed into something new, signalling a rearrangement of the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone gets a wake-up call while taking up a hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges the letters of A MORNING CALL BOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancing waltzes and foxtrots in pairs is a popular pastime and hobby.

clue.text: Tom, say, getting a set of items, we hear — engineer of change?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, given by example

indicators.note: we hear signals that the letters are spelt as the word for a set of items sounds when spoken

parts.note: a list is a series of items

explanation.surface: A man named Tom gets a collection of things and becomes the driver of reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a person's name but is a tomcat. 'we hear' gives LYST, sounding like LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalyst is something that brings about or speeds up a transformation.

clue.text: Tree and lake overlooking curved structure

indicators.note: in a down answer, overlooking means the letter for lake sits above the arch

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
an arch is a curved span

explanation.surface: A tree and a lake looking out over an arched bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The larch is a deciduous conifer, a species of tree.

clue.text: Part's sure to be rewritten for celebrity

indicators.note: rewritten means the letters are written out again in a new order

explanation.surface: An actor is told their role will be redrafted for a famous star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be rewritten' rearranges PARTS and SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A superstar is a hugely famous performer, a very big name.

clue.text: I dust a loft to be converted in restrictive accommodation

indicators.note: converted means changed into a different form, as a loft conversion changes a room, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone cleaning an attic space before a builder converts it into a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be converted' rearranges I DUST A LOFT; the loft conversion surface is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio flat is a one-room apartment, cramped living quarters.

clue.text: Defective work taking place in railway

indicators.note: taking place in means the work's letters sit inside the railway's

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Faulty engineering works going on along the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropy is informal British for poor-quality or shoddy.

clue.text: Crack Northern priest in US city for retirement

indicators.note: in means the priest and northern letters sit inside the turned-round city
for retirement means the city name goes backwards, retiring or withdrawing

parts.note: Reno is a city in Nevada
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A broken northern clergyman goes to an American city to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: Crack here means a quip, not a break; the priest is the Old Testament Eli.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a witty quip, and a one-liner is a short joke.

clue.text: Earl excited around house in Asian city

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters surround the abbreviation for house
excited means stirred up, so the letters of the word Earl are jumbled

explanation.surface: An aristocrat gets worked up as he moves through a mansion in an Asian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lahore is a major city in Pakistan, capital of Punjab province.

clue.text: Depressed college athlete

definitions.meaning: someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge university at a sport

explanation.definitionFit: Blue means melancholy; an Oxbridge sportsman awarded colours is called a Blue.

clue.text: Inn loud lad disrupted I abandoned in Welsh place

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters of the first three words are scrambled
abandoned says the letter I is left out of the scrambled pool

explanation.surface: A noisy young man causes chaos in a pub and someone gets left behind in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of INN LOUD LAD, remove I ('I abandoned'), and rearrange ('disrupted') the remaining nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Llandudno is a seaside resort town in north Wales.

clue.text: Former student thus allowed close to college and past it

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil
so means thus
let means allowed

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An ex-pupil, given permission to return near the college, is past his prime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' picks the last letter, E, of college.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsolete means outdated and no longer useful, like something past its best.

clue.text: Dissolute character in family cut by warring tribe

indicators.note: cut by means the family word is split open by the other letters

parts.note: line means lineage or family

indicators.note: warring means in conflict and disorder, so the letters of tribe are mixed up

explanation.surface: A depraved person within a clan is attacked by a hostile tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A libertine is a person who lives a promiscuous, morally unrestrained life.

clue.text: Strategic conversation almost about part of play I caught

indicators.note: about means the shortened word surrounds the other letters
almost means the word for conversation loses its final letter

parts.note: talk means conversation
an act is a division of a play
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A tactical chat nearly concerning a section of a play the speaker took in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TALK to TAL, which goes 'about' ACT, I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactical means relating to planned manoeuvres, close in sense to strategic.

clue.text: Romantic novelist showing craft in family with daughter

indicators.note: in means the craft word sits inside the family word

parts.note: a clan is an extended family
art means skill or craft

explanation.surface: A writer of love stories displays her skill among relatives with her daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbara Cartland was a prolific British romance writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbara Cartland wrote hundreds of love stories, making her a famous romance author.

clue.text: Noise from boxer, say, giving natural protection

definitions.meaning: the sound a dog such as a boxer makes
the tough outer covering of a tree

explanation.definitionFit: A boxer dog makes a woof, and a tree trunk is shielded by its outer layer.

clue.text: Decorative work from firm after reversing economy measures

indicators.note: after means the firm's letters come behind the turned-round word
reversing means the word for economy measures runs backwards

parts.note: cuts are reductions in spending
CO is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Ornamental plasterwork produced by a company after it undoes spending cutbacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is fine plaster used for ornamental mouldings on walls and ceilings.

clue.text: Bad diction encapsulating compulsive fan

indicators.note: encapsulating means the phrase before it holds the answer's letters inside it

explanation.surface: Poor pronunciation surrounding an obsessive enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encapsulating' says the letters run inside 'Bad diction'.
explanation.definitionFit: An addict is a devotee, someone hooked on a pastime or substance.

clue.text: Coastline feature favoured by rental property

parts.note: in means in favour, favoured
a let is a property rented out

explanation.surface: A seaside feature that is popular with holiday rentals.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is a narrow arm of the sea cutting into the shore.

clue.text: One's happy to have shed habit?

definitions.text: One's happy to have shed habit?

parts.words: One's happy to have shed habit?
parts.note: suggests someone such as a nun glad to give up a habit, but it is a person glad to remove their clothes

explanation.surface: Someone delighted to have given up a bad habit, or a nun leaving her order.
explanation.walkthrough: Habit means clothing, as a monk's or nun's robe, not a routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist is a nudist, someone happy to go without clothing.

clue.text: Discharge some proposal voluntarily

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Release some suggestion that is offered freely.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous firing of guns, a discharge of artillery.

clue.text: Star member of Python team mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the answer is spelt as the comedian's surname sounds

parts.note: Eric Idle was one of the Monty Python comedy troupe

explanation.surface: A celebrity from the Monty Python comedy group is name-checked.
explanation.walkthrough: Monty Python was a British comedy team; Eric Idle was one member.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an adored celebrity, a star with fans.

clue.text: Fur needed when getting cold in populous country

indicators.note: getting means the country takes the chilly word into itself

parts.note: China has one of the world's largest populations
chill means cold

explanation.surface: Warm furs are needed when it turns cold in a crowded country.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinchilla is the soft grey pelt of a small Andean rodent.

clue.text: March round lots possibly in obscure conditions

indicators.note: in means the round letter and jumbled letters sit inside the fog

parts.note: fog is weather that obscures vision
O is round in shape

indicators.note: possibly means the word lots might be rearranged

explanation.surface: A march going round a great many things, perhaps through murky weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges LOTS, here as OTSL, and with O it goes 'in' FOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Footslog means to trudge a long way on foot, as on a weary march.

clue.text: Love shown by Anglican group for wild cat

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O
CE stands for Church of England
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: Affection displayed by a church congregation for a wild animal.
explanation.walkthrough: CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a spotted wild cat of the Americas.
